passage.title: A new café on the high street
paras: Amir and Sara want to open a café on their local high street. They have both worked in cafés for five years and want to run their own business, sharing the work and the profit equally.

The fit-out and equipment (coffee machine, ovens, fridges, tables) will cost about £40,000. They have £15,000 of savings between them; the rest must come from investors or other sources. Both own their homes.
A café on this street has closed twice in the last three years. Amir would like the business to look established to suppliers; Sara would like to keep the accounts private and the paperwork simple.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.text: Justify whether Amir and Sara should form a partnership or a private limited company. (9 marks)

frame.label: Because (use the data)

frame.label: Overall, why my choice beats it
frame.prompt: Compare the two: why your option is better for THIS business.

markScheme.q: Justify: partnership or private limited company (9)
markScheme.a: Either, if justified. Ltd: limited liability protects their homes, important as two cafés have closed on this street and £25,000 is needed beyond savings; looks established to suppliers. Partnership: simpler and cheaper to set up, accounts private (Sara's wish). Best answers weigh risk against cost and privacy for this café. Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice that uses the data, with developed chains of reasoning and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons for the choice in context but little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.
